title: ESP-NOW Messenger
intro: Send messages between two boards with no router. Press a button and your friend's board buzzes.

wiring_steps.title: The button
wiring_steps.text: Unplug the USB cable before you change any wires. Plug it back in when you're done. You and a friend each build this circuit on your own ESP32. Start with the power rails: a black wire from GND on your board to the blue (−) rail at the bottom of the breadboard, and a red wire from {{VCC}} to the red (+) rail. Press the button into the middle of the breadboard so it sits across the gap: its legs go in F4, F6, E4 and E6. Add a wire from {{pin:BUTTON_PIN}} to J4, and a black wire from A6 to the blue (−) rail. (The code turns on the pin's pull-up, so no resistor is needed.)

wiring_steps.title: The LED
wiring_steps.text: Push the LED into holes H12 and H13, with the long leg (+) in H13. Put a 220Ω resistor from G12 across the gap to E12. Add a wire from {{pin:LED_PIN}} to J13, and a black wire from A12 to the blue (−) rail at the bottom.

wiring_steps.title: The buzzer
wiring_steps.text: The buzzer sits beside the breadboard. Connect its + leg (the red wire, or the leg marked +) to {{pin:BUZZER_PIN}}, and its − leg (the black wire) to the blue (−) rail.

steps.title: Your board's address
steps.text:
Every WiFi chip has its own **MAC address**: six numbers, like a name tag, written in hexadecimal (`3C:71:BF:4A:12:F0`).

**Your task:** Upload to both boards and write down each board's MAC address.
hints: Open the Serial Monitor after uploading.
If nothing shows, press the board's EN (reset) button.
steps.success: Every board has its own address. ESP-NOW uses it to send messages.

steps.title: Send a message
steps.text:
ESP-NOW sends short messages straight to other boards, with no router. Sending to `FF:FF:FF:FF:FF:FF` **broadcasts**: every board nearby hears it.

**Your task:** fill in the blank to send the message when the button is pressed. Upload to both boards.
hints: Who should get the message? Everyone.
steps.success: Your board is sending. Next, make the other board listen.

steps.title: Buzz your friend
steps.text: **Goal:** both boards run the same code. Pressing your button makes your friend's board light its LED and beep (and theirs does the same to yours).
hints: `esp_now_register_recv_cb(received);` tells ESP-NOW which function to run when a message arrives.
Don't beep inside the receive function: set a `volatile bool` and beep in `loop()`.
The receive function needs exactly these inputs: `(const esp_now_recv_info_t* info, const uint8_t* data, int length)`.

checks.label: My friend's board buzzes when I press

steps.success: You built a wireless messenger with no router at all!

outro: Your boards talk directly to each other with **ESP-NOW**: no router, no internet. Every board has a **MAC address**, a name for its WiFi chip, and messages are **broadcast** to every board nearby.
stretch: Send how many times you've pressed, and show it on your friend's Serial Monitor.
Send Morse code: short and long presses make short and long beeps.
Give each board a name, and show who sent each message.
